findingRule: Separate audited waste, proven criminal action, investigated allegations and policy disputes. Any link to fares or tolls requires a documented budget and causal trace. No personal surcharge estimates are derived from project totals.

pathways.title: Who raised fares or tolls?
pathways.ask: Which board voted on the rate, what fiscal gap or capital plan was cited, and where did the additional revenue go?

sources.label: Port Authority toll rates and policy

pathways.title: Did public contracting waste money?
pathways.ask: Were contracts competitively awarded, properly priced, delivered and audited? Were taxpayers or riders reimbursed?

sources.label: Port Authority report fraud and procurement concerns

pathways.title: Did donors, vendors or powerful investors benefit?
pathways.ask: Were there financial ties to awarded vendors or decision-makers, and is the timing tied to a verified decision?
needed: public contract ID and purchasing decision

pathways.title: Did the problem actually raise a fare?
pathways.ask: What contract cost flowed into which budget, and did the rate-setting body identify that cost in the adopted fare or toll decision?
needed: matched contract and audited excess cost
rider exposure and dated fare table

examples.name: Amtrak renovation contract kickbacks
examples.finding: DOT OIG reported a $7,257,232 civil resolution with a contractor and its owner following kickbacks, prior guilty pleas by executives, and more than $2 million in improper Amtrak contract billing.
examples.amountMeaning: More than $2 million improperly billed to Amtrak, not a passenger cost calculation.
examples.unproven: No direct dollar effect on any passenger ticket price has been measured; not a local subway or road toll case.

examples.name: MBTA warehousing contract overpayments
examples.finding: Massachusetts OIG found MBTA reduced a vendor's contractual obligations without reducing the paid contract rates and inadequately monitored performance in earlier years.
examples.amountMeaning: No amount asserted here because the linked summary does not provide a comparable verified total.
examples.unproven: Poor contract oversight is evidenced; fraud, bribery and a fare increase caused by this contract are not established by this audit.

examples.name: MTA procurement conflict disclosed by Inspector General
examples.finding: The MTA Inspector General described an inappropriate relationship between an MTA procurement officer and a vendor sales agent associated with millions of dollars in purchases.
examples.amountMeaning: The Inspector General's summary does not quantify any resulting extra passenger fare.
examples.unproven: Do not infer a particular agency fare increase or a company-specific overcharge from the summary alone.

examples.name: MBTA track-inspection and overtime allegations
examples.finding: Federal authorities charged current and former MBTA employees over alleged falsified Red Line track inspection reports and fraudulent overtime.
examples.unproven: Charges are allegations; defendants are presumed innocent. No fare impact has been substantiated.

scope: Cases are illustrative nationwide transportation governance investigations, not accusations about the fare or toll operator a visitor actually uses. No implied corruption based only on a rate increase.
